name: Pico Genesis / PicoSure Pro

lead: PicoSure Pro is a picosecond 755 nm alexandrite laser made by Cynosure that dermatology clinics use for acne scars, pigmentation and tattoo work. "Pico Genesis" appears in appearance forums and clinic menus as a name for picosecond-style skin treatments.

Published research on the PicoSure Pro for appearance is limited. A small prospective study has looked at it combined with radiofrequency microneedling for atrophic acne scars, and a 23-person post-market usability trial has been registered.

paras: Picosecond lasers deliver energy in trillionths of a second. Proponents describe this as acting through a mainly photomechanical rather than purely heat-based effect, and a diffractive lens array can be added to produce small zones of skin change for scars and texture.

Treatments are performed in clinics and are generally described as having short-lived redness and swelling; pigment changes are a recognised concern with laser treatments of skin, especially in darker skin types. Long-term comparative data are scarce.

trials.title: Post Market Usability Evaluation Of The PicoSure Pro Device

lead: PicoSure Pro is a picosecond laser system from Cynosure that emits light at 755 nm (an alexandrite laser) and can be fitted with a diffractive lens array. It is used in dermatology and aesthetic clinics for conditions such as atrophic acne scarring, wrinkles and pigmented lesions. [1][2]

"Pico Genesis" is a name used in clinic and forum discussion of picosecond skin treatments; this article treats it together with PicoSure Pro, the device for which published research and trial registrations could be found.

Published evidence for appearance outcomes is limited to small studies. A 2025 prospective single-center study evaluated the PicoSure Pro with a diffractive lens array combined with radiofrequency microneedling for facial atrophic acne scars [1], and a completed 23-participant post-market usability trial was registered for wrinkles, acne scars and benign pigmented lesions [2].

paras: The device is described in the research literature for facial atrophic acne scarring when used with a diffractive lens array, and a registered usability trial listed wrinkles, acne scars, and benign epidermal and dermal pigmented lesions as conditions of interest. [1][2]

A prospective, single-center study published in Dermatologic Surgery in 2025 evaluated combination treatment with the PicoSure Pro and a radiofrequency microneedling device (Potenza) for atrophic acne scars. [1]

A post-market usability evaluation of the PicoSure Pro (NCT05102617), started in October 2021 with 23 participants, is registered as completed; it lists wrinkles, acne scars and benign pigmented lesions as conditions. [2]

Earlier laboratory work examined skin histology after treatment with a picosecond alexandrite laser and a fractional lens array.  The small sample sizes and lack of long-term comparison data limit what can be concluded.

Picosecond laser treatments are discussed in appearance communities as a skin-quality procedure (scars, pigment, texture). Little community material was available for this entry, and it is categorised under "hardmaxx" procedures.
